blocks.text: Expose a form controller that accepts initial values, typed validation, a durable local repository, an optional versioned remote adapter, and an idempotent submit callback. Consumers render steps while the controller owns restore, autosave, conflict, and navigation state.

Contract checks:
- Local persistence and remote synchronization have separate adapters and outcomes.
- Remote writes carry base revision, idempotency key, generation, and AbortSignal.
- Save status distinguishes local durability from remote acknowledgement.
- Restore, conflict resolution, discard, and submission are explicit commands.

blocks.title: Core interfaces
rows: A complete clean baseline prevents ambiguous missing fields during migration and reset.
The repository owns storage technology, schema parsing, atomic replacement, quota errors, and deletion.
Remote sync remains optional but, when present, uses explicit revision, idempotency, cancellation, and conflict outcomes.
Submission is separate from autosave and clears drafts only after confirmed success.
A meaningful local/remote divergence cannot be erased by an implicit last-write-wins rule.
{ values, formUi, save, setField, goToStep, submit, resolveConflict, discardDraft }
The view can distinguish field interaction, local save, remote conflict, navigation, and final submission.

blocks.title: Required public behavior
items: A stable draft identity and durable local repository.
Step and full-form validation over one FormModel.
An optional remote adapter with revision and cancellation contracts.
Explicit restore, conflict-resolution, discard, and submit commands.
A controller result exposing values, navigation, errors, save state, and recovery actions.

blocks.title: Keep outside the API
items: Forcing consumers to manually call localStorage.setItem.
Returning different shapes depending on step (inconsistent contracts).
Hiding validation behind magic: callers can’t plug in their own rules.
Mixing UI details (progress bar rendering) into the core form API.
Making submit fire even when some steps are invalid (undefined behavior).

steps.title: 1. Create draft-aware controller
steps.text: The page creates the form controller with a draft ID, local repository, optional remote adapter, initial values, validation, and submit command. Initialization compares validated local and remote drafts before choosing a base.

steps.title: 2. Edit & validate
steps.text: Inputs call setFieldValue (or onChange props), which updates the form model and sets dirty = true. Inline validation uses validateStep to populate validationErrors.

steps.title: 3. Write local, then optional remote draft
steps.text: The coordinator writes a versioned local envelope for the captured generation, then optionally starts a remote save with its base revision and AbortSignal. Each outcome updates only the matching generation.

steps.title: 4. Step navigation
steps.text: nextStep() runs validateStep for the current step; if there are no errors it increments currentStep. prevStep() just decrements (no validation needed).

steps.title: 5. Submit idempotent final values
steps.text: When submit() is called, the component runs full validation (all steps). On success it calls onSubmit(form) and clears the draft key. On failure it surfaces errors without losing any data.

items.label: Public surface
items.helperText: A small set of props and helpers that stay stable over time.

items.label: Data direction
items.helperText: Consumers configure behavior; the form reports events and results.

items.label: Strong signal
items.helperText: You clearly define how drafts are created, restored and discarded.

blocks.title: Contract checkpoint
blocks.text: A good API makes complex behavior (multi-step + autosave + validation) feel simple to use. If another engineer can wire this form into their page just from the props and hook signatures you described, you’ve nailed the interface.

Draft reads and writes include schema and remote revisions. A remote save uses a precondition and returns the new revision. The UI aborts obsolete transport work when possible but still rejects stale generations. Submission is a separate idempotent command and successful completion clears only the matching draft identity.

steps.title: Capture field change
steps.text: Update field state and mark one path dirty without validating unrelated steps.

steps.title: Schedule captured generation
steps.text: Debounce storage work from input and flush at safe navigation boundaries.

steps.title: Commit draft envelope
steps.text: Write an atomic local envelope, then reconcile a versioned remote draft if enabled.

steps.title: Finalize form
steps.text: Run final validation, send one idempotent command, and clear the draft only after success.
